name: Dropbox
description: Dropbox is a cloud storage service offering file syncing, sharing, and collaboration across devices with version control and robust integrations

tools.name: Activate team folder
tools.description: Tool to activate an archived team folder. Use when you need to restore access to a previously archived team folder.

inputs.name: team_folder_id
inputs.about: The ID of the team folder to activate.

tools.name: Add file member
tools.description: Tool to add specified members to a Dropbox file with configurable access levels. Use when sharing a file with specific users by email or Dropbox ID. Supports custom invitation messages and notification controls. Note: This endpoint does not support apps with the app folder permission, and members will receive invitations unless quiet mode is enabled.

inputs.name: file
inputs.about: File to which to add members. Use the file ID format (e.g., 'id:7bh4zBmgZoAAAAAAAAABCQ') or file path.

inputs.name: quiet
inputs.about: Whether to suppress device notifications for added members. If false (default), members will be notified of their invitation.

inputs.name: members
inputs.about: List of members to add to the file. Each member is identified by email or Dropbox ID. Note: If an email is provided and it's the user's main account email, they may be directly added to the membership.

inputs.name: access_level
inputs.about: Defines the access level for the new member.

inputs.name: custom_message
inputs.about: Custom message to include in the invitation email sent to added members.

inputs.name: add_message_as_comment
inputs.about: If true and a custom_message is provided, the message will be added as a comment on the file.

tools.name: Add file properties
tools.description: Tool to add custom properties to a Dropbox file using a filled property template. Use when you need to tag files with structured metadata like project info, status, or categories.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: A unique identifier for the file or folder. Can be a file path (e.g., '/test.txt') or a file ID (e.g., 'id:a4ayc_80_OEAAAAAAAAAXw').

inputs.name: property_groups
inputs.about: The property groups to be added to the Dropbox file. Each group must reference a valid template that the file doesn't already have.

inputs.name: Dropbox-API-Select-User
inputs.about: Team member ID (format: dbmid:...) required when using team tokens. Specifies which team member's account to operate on.

tools.name: Add tag to file or folder
tools.description: Tool to add a tag to a file or folder in Dropbox. Use when you need to tag items for organization. Tags are automatically converted to lowercase.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: Path to the file or folder to tag. Must be a valid path in the user's Dropbox.

inputs.name: tag_text
inputs.about: The tag text to add. Will be automatically converted to lowercase letters by Dropbox.

inputs.name: Dropbox-API-Select-User
inputs.about: Team member ID (format: dbmid:...) required when using team tokens. Specifies which team member's account to operate on.

tools.name: Add folder member
tools.description: Tool to add members to a shared folder with specified access levels. Use when an owner or editor needs to invite new members to a shared folder. Members receive invites and must be mounted via mount_folder for full access. Requires appropriate ACL permissions.

inputs.name: quiet
inputs.about: Whether to suppress email and device notifications for the added members. If true, members are added silently without notification. Default is false

inputs.name: members
inputs.about: List of members to add to the shared folder. Each member will receive an invitation to join the folder

inputs.name: custom_message
inputs.about: Optional custom message to include in the invitation email sent to added members

inputs.name: shared_folder_id
inputs.about: The ID of the shared folder to add members to. You can get this from list_shared_folders action

tools.name: Add users to space limits exclusion list
tools.description: Tool to add users to the team's space limits exclusion list in Dropbox. Users on this list are exempt from space limit restrictions. Use when you need to exclude specific team members from storage quota enforcement. Requires team admin authentication.

inputs.name: users
inputs.about: List of users to be added to the space limits exclusion list. Each user can be specified by team_member_id, external_id, or email. Maximum size of the list is 1000 users.

tools.name: Add sharing allowlist
tools.description: Tool to add domains or email addresses to the team sharing allowlist. Use when team admins need to approve specific domains or emails for sharing. Requires team admin authentication. At least one of 'domains' or 'emails' must be provided, with a maximum of 100 entries per call.

inputs.name: emails
inputs.about: List of email addresses to add to the allowlist. Each email must be a valid string representation following RFC-5322/822 (e.g., 'user@example.com'). Maximum 100 entries per call. At least one of 'domains' or 'emails' must be provided

inputs.name: domains
inputs.about: List of domains to add to the allowlist. Each domain must be a valid string representation following RFC-1034/5 (e.g., 'example.com', 'subdomain.example.org'). Maximum 100 entries per call. At least one of 'domains' or 'emails' must be provided

tools.name: Add members to team group
tools.description: Tool to add members to a team group with specified access levels. Use when you need to add users to an existing team group. Requires team admin credentials with group management permissions.

inputs.name: group
inputs.about: The group to add members to. Use group_id obtained from list_team_groups or create_team_group actions

inputs.name: members
inputs.about: List of members to add to the group with their respective access levels

inputs.name: return_members
inputs.about: Whether to return the list of members in the group after adding. Default is true

tools.name: Add team members
tools.description: Add up to 20 new members to a Dropbox team with specified roles and settings; requires team admin credentials. The operation may return an asynchronous job ID or complete with per-member results.

inputs.name: force_async
inputs.about: Whether to force the operation to happen asynchronously. If true, returns an async_job_id to poll for completion. Default is false

inputs.name: new_members
inputs.about: List of new members to add to the team. Maximum of 20 members per request

tools.name: Add secondary emails to team members
tools.description: Tool to add secondary email addresses to Dropbox team members. Use when you need to associate additional email addresses with team member accounts. Requires team admin credentials.

inputs.name: new_secondary_emails
inputs.about: List of users and their secondary emails to add. Each entry specifies a user (by ID or email) and the secondary emails to add for them

tools.name: Add property template for team
tools.description: Tool to add a property template for a team in Dropbox. Use when you need to create a standardized set of custom properties that can be applied to files and folders. Requires team admin permissions and a Dropbox Business account.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Display name for the template. Template names can be up to 256 bytes.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: Definitions of the property fields associated with this template. There can be up to 32 properties in a single template.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Description for the template. Template descriptions can be up to 1024 bytes.

tools.name: Alpha Upload File
tools.description: Tool to upload a new file to Dropbox using the alpha upload endpoint. Use when uploading files up to 150 MiB. Note that the behavior of this alpha endpoint is unstable and subject to change.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.about: Selects what to do if the file already exists.

inputs.name: mute
inputs.about: If true, this tells the clients that this modification shouldn't result in a user notification.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: Path in the user's Dropbox to save the file. Must start with '/' and include the filename.

inputs.name: content
inputs.about: File to be uploaded. Supports various formats including text, images, and PDFs.

inputs.name: autorename
inputs.about: If there's a conflict as determined by mode, have the Dropbox server try to autorename the file to avoid conflict.

inputs.name: client_modified
inputs.about: The value to store as the client_modified timestamp in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2015-05-12T15:50:38Z'). Dropbox automatically records the time at which the file was written to the Dropbox servers.

inputs.name: property_groups
inputs.about: List of custom properties to add to file.

inputs.name: dropbox_api_select_user
inputs.about: Optional. For team accounts: Dropbox account ID or team member ID to operate on. Required when using a Dropbox Business team token. Format: 'dbid:...' or team_member_id.

tools.name: Append data to upload session
tools.description: Tool to append more data to an existing upload session. Use when uploading large files in chunks. When the 'close' parameter is set to true, this call will close the session. A single request should not upload more than 150 MiB.

inputs.name: close
inputs.about: If true, the upload session will be closed after appending this data. Once closed, no more data can be appended to the session.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: Cursor information containing the session_id and current offset in bytes.

inputs.name: content
inputs.about: File data to append to the upload session.

tools.name: Append to multiple upload sessions
tools.description: Tool to append data to multiple upload sessions in a single request. Use when you need to upload data to multiple ongoing upload sessions efficiently. The file content for each session should be concatenated in the request body in the order specified by entries. A single request should not upload more than 150 MiB. The maximum size of a file one can upload to an upload session is 2^41 - 2^22 (2,199,019,061,248) bytes.

inputs.name: data
inputs.about: Concatenated binary data for all upload sessions. The data for each session should be concatenated in the order specified in the entries list. Each chunk's length must match the corresponding entry's length field.

inputs.name: entries
inputs.about: List of upload session entries to append data to. Each entry specifies the session, how many bytes to read from the request body, and whether to close the session. The data for each entry should be concatenated in the request body in the same order as this list.

tools.name: Archive team folder
tools.description: Tool to archive an active team folder in Dropbox. Sets the team folder's status to archived and removes all folder and file members. Use when you need to archive a team folder that is no longer in active use. The folder must be active before it can be archived.

inputs.name: team_folder_id
inputs.about: The ID of the team folder to archive. You can get this from list team folders action. The team folder must be active to be archived.

inputs.name: force_async_off
inputs.about: Whether to force the operation to run synchronously. If true, the operation will complete synchronously and return metadata immediately. If false or not specified, large operations may complete asynchronously.

tools.name: Check copy batch job status
tools.description: Check the status of an asynchronous Dropbox copy batch job using its job ID. Returns an in-progress, complete, failed, or polling-error status; complete responses may include per-entry results.

inputs.name: async_job_id
inputs.about: Id of the asynchronous job. This is the value of a response returned from the method that launched the job.

tools.name: Check delete batch status
tools.description: Tool to check the status of an asynchronous delete batch job in Dropbox. Use when you need to poll the status of a batch delete operation initiated by delete_batch. Returns 'in_progress', 'complete' with per-entry results, 'failed', or error status.

inputs.name: async_job_id
inputs.about: Id of the asynchronous job. This is the value of a response returned from the method that launched the job.

tools.name: Check folder batch status
tools.description: Check the status of an asynchronous Dropbox folder batch creation job using its job ID. Returns an in-progress, complete, failed, or polling-error status; complete responses may include per-entry results.

inputs.name: async_job_id
inputs.about: ID of the asynchronous job. This is the value returned from the create_folder_batch method.

tools.name: Check sharing job status
tools.description: Tool to check the status of an asynchronous sharing job in Dropbox. Use when you have an async_job_id from a previous sharing operation (like unshare_folder, remove_folder_member) and need to poll its status. Returns 'in_progress', 'complete', 'failed' with error details, or polling errors.

inputs.name: async_job_id
inputs.about: Id of the asynchronous job. This is the value of a response returned from the method that launched the job.

tools.name: Check move batch job status
tools.description: Tool to check the status of an asynchronous move batch job. Use when you need to poll the status of a batch move operation started with move_batch_v2. Returns a list of results for each entry when complete.

inputs.name: async_job_id
inputs.about: Id of the asynchronous job. This is the value of a response returned from the method that launched the job.

tools.name: Check move former member files job status
tools.description: Tool to check the status of an asynchronous move former member files job. Use when you have an async_job_id from a previous team/members/move_former_member_files operation and need to poll its completion status. Returns 'in_progress', 'complete', 'failed' with error details, or error states like 'invalid_async_job_id'.

inputs.name: async_job_id
inputs.about: Id of the asynchronous job returned from team/members/move_former_member_files. This is used to poll the status of the file move operation.

tools.name: Check remove member job status
tools.description: Tool to check the status of an asynchronous remove folder member job in Dropbox. Use when you have an async_job_id from a previous remove_folder_member operation and need to poll its status. Returns 'in_progress', 'complete' with access level info, or 'failed' with error details.

inputs.name: async_job_id
inputs.about: Id of the asynchronous job. This is the value of a response returned from the method that launched the job.

tools.name: Check save URL job status
tools.description: Tool to check the status of a save_url job in Dropbox. Use when you have an async_job_id from a save_url operation and need to poll its completion status. Returns 'in_progress', 'complete' with file metadata, or 'failed' with error details.

inputs.name: async_job_id
inputs.about: The async job ID returned from a previous save_url operation.

tools.name: Check share job status
tools.description: Tool to check the status of an asynchronous folder sharing job in Dropbox. Use when you need to poll the status of a folder share operation that was initiated asynchronously. Returns 'in_progress', 'complete' with folder metadata, 'failed' with error details, or polling error status.

inputs.name: async_job_id
inputs.about: Id of the asynchronous job. This is the value of a response returned from the method that launched the job.

tools.name: Check team folder archive status
tools.description: Tool to check the status of an asynchronous team folder archive job in Dropbox. Use when you have an async_job_id from a previous team_folder/archive operation and need to poll its status. Returns 'in_progress' while archiving, 'complete' with team folder metadata when done, or error states like 'invalid_async_job_id'.

inputs.name: async_job_id
inputs.about: Id of the asynchronous job returned from the team_folder/archive method that launched the archive operation.

tools.name: Check upload batch status
tools.description: Check the status of an asynchronous Dropbox upload batch job initiated by upload_session/finish_batch. Poll using the job ID to see whether it is still in progress, has completed with per-entry results, or has returned a polling error.

inputs.name: async_job_id
inputs.about: Id of the asynchronous job. This is the value of a response returned from the method that launched the job.

tools.name: Check user
tools.description: Tool to test Dropbox API connection and validate access token by echoing back a supplied string. Use when you need to verify that the Dropbox API is accessible and the access token is valid.

inputs.name: query
inputs.about: The string that you'd like to be echoed back to you. Maximum length is 500 characters.

tools.name: Copy multiple files or folders
tools.description: Tool to copy multiple files or folders to different locations at once in Dropbox. Use when you need to duplicate multiple items efficiently. This operation may complete synchronously or return a job ID for async processing. Use copy_batch/check:2 to check async job status.

inputs.name: entries
inputs.about: List of entries to be copied. Each entry is a RelocationPath with from_path and to_path.

inputs.name: autorename
inputs.about: If there's a conflict with any file, have the Dropbox server try to autorename that file to avoid the conflict. The default is false.

inputs.name: dropbox_api_select_user
inputs.about: Team member ID (format: dbmid:...) required when using team tokens. Specifies which team member's account to operate on.

tools.name: Copy file or folder
tools.description: Tool to copy a file or folder to a different location in Dropbox. Use when you need to duplicate content without removing the original. If the source path is a folder, all its contents will be copied.

inputs.name: to_path
inputs.about: Path in the user's Dropbox that is the destination. This path is case-sensitive.

inputs.name: from_path
inputs.about: Path in the user's Dropbox to be copied. This path is case-sensitive.

inputs.name: autorename
inputs.about: If there's a conflict (e.g., a file with the same name already exists at the destination), have the Dropbox server try to auto-rename the file to avoid the conflict. The default is false.

inputs.name: allow_shared_folder
inputs.about: If true, allows copying of shared folders. Note: This flag has no effect in current API version. The default is false.

inputs.name: dropbox_api_select_user
inputs.about: Team member ID (format: dbmid:...) required when using team tokens. Specifies which team member's account to operate on.

inputs.name: allow_ownership_transfer
inputs.about: Allow moves by owner even if it would result in an ownership transfer for the content being moved. Note: This does not apply to copies. The default is false.

tools.name: Count file requests
tools.description: Tool to get the total number of file requests owned by the authenticated user. Use when you need to count how many file requests (both open and closed) exist.

tools.name: Create file request
tools.description: Tool to create a new file request in Dropbox. Use when you need to request files from others by generating a unique link for uploads to a specified Dropbox folder, optionally with a deadline.

inputs.name: open
inputs.about: Whether the file request should be open by default. If true, the file request will start accepting files immediately.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the new file request. Must be 1 character or more.

inputs.name: deadline
inputs.about: Represents the deadline parameters for a file request.

inputs.name: destination
inputs.about: The path in the user's Dropbox where uploaded files will be saved. Must be a path starting with '/'. Example: '/Homework/math'

tools.name: Create folder
tools.description: Tool to create a new folder at a specified path in Dropbox. Use when you need to organize files by creating a new directory.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: Path in the user's Dropbox to create the folder. Must start with a slash. May use 'id:' prefix for namespace-based paths. Must not end with '/' or whitespace. Paths are case-insensitive but must be correctly formatted to avoid validation errors.

inputs.name: autorename
inputs.about: If there's a conflict, have the Dropbox server try to autorename the folder to avoid the conflict. Default is False. Without autorename, a conflict returns a `path_conflict` error. For idempotent folder creation, set autorename=true or treat `path_conflict` as non-fatal.

tools.name: Create multiple folders
tools.description: Create multiple folders in Dropbox in a single request. The operation can return results synchronously or an asynchronous job ID for checking completion.

inputs.name: paths
inputs.about: List of paths to be created in the user's Dropbox. Each path must start with a slash. Duplicate path arguments in the batch are considered only once. Maximum 10,000 paths.

inputs.name: autorename
inputs.about: If there's a conflict, have the Dropbox server try to autorename the folder to avoid the conflict. Default is False.

inputs.name: force_async
inputs.about: Whether to force the create to happen asynchronously. For large batches, the operation will be asynchronous automatically. Default is False.

tools.name: Create paper document
tools.description: Creates a new Dropbox Paper document at the specified path using HTML or Markdown content.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The fully qualified path in Dropbox where the Paper document will be created. MUST include the .paper extension at the end (e.g., '/My Documents/Notes.paper').

inputs.name: content
inputs.about: Content of the paper document

inputs.name: import_format
inputs.about: Format of the provided content

tools.name: Create Paper folder
tools.description: Tool to create a new Paper folder with the provided info. Use when you need to organize Paper documents by creating a new folder. Note: This endpoint works for content created by users on the older version of Paper.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the new Paper folder.

inputs.name: is_team_folder
inputs.about: Whether the folder to be created should be a team folder. If not specified, defaults to false.

inputs.name: parent_folder_id
inputs.about: The encrypted Paper folder Id where the new Paper folder should be created. If not provided, the folder will be created at the root level.

tools.name: Create shared link
tools.description: Tool to create a stable, long-lived shared link for a Dropbox file or folder. Use when the user needs a permanent URL suitable for embedding or long-term sharing (as opposed to temporary links that expire in hours). Supports optional settings like expiration, password protection, and visibility controls. Note: If a shared link already exists for the path, the API will return an error; in that case, use a separate list_shared_links endpoint to retrieve existing links.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path or file identifier to be shared by the shared link. Supports Dropbox path (e.g., '/folder/file.txt'), id:..., rev:..., or ns:... notation.

inputs.name: settings
inputs.about: Settings for the shared link configuration.

tools.name: Create simple shared link (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use CreateSharedLinkV2 instead. Tool to create a basic shared link for a Dropbox file or folder. If a shared link already exists for the given path, that link is returned. Use when you need a simple shared link without advanced settings like password protection or custom expiration. For links with advanced settings, use the create_shared_link action instead.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path to share. This can be a file or folder path in Dropbox (e.g., '/folder/file.txt'). If a shared link already exists for this path, that link will be returned instead of creating a new one.

inputs.name: short_url
inputs.about: Whether to return a shortened URL. If true, the returned URL will be shorter and easier to share.

inputs.name: pending_upload
inputs.about: Mode for pending upload indicating file or folder type.

tools.name: Create team folder
tools.description: Tool to create a new, active team folder with no members in Dropbox. Use when you need to set up a new team folder for collaboration. The folder is created without any members initially.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Name for the new team folder. The name must be unique within the team.

inputs.name: sync_setting
inputs.about: Sync setting enum for the team folder.

tools.name: Create team group
tools.description: Tool to create a new, empty team group in Dropbox with a specified name. Use when you need to create a new group for organizing team members. Requires team admin credentials with team member management permissions.

inputs.name: group_name
inputs.about: The name for the new group. Must not be empty.

inputs.name: group_external_id
inputs.about: An arbitrary external ID that the creator of the team can associate with the group for organizational purposes.

inputs.name: group_management_type
inputs.about: The type of group management for the team group.

tools.name: Delete all closed file requests
tools.description: Tool to delete all closed file requests owned by the current user. Use when you need to clean up closed file requests in bulk.

tools.name: Delete multiple files/folders
tools.description: Delete multiple files or folders in Dropbox in one batch. The operation may return complete results immediately or an asynchronous job ID that can be checked for completion.

inputs.name: entries
inputs.about: List of files or folders to delete. Maximum 1000 entries per request.

tools.name: Delete file or folder
tools.description: Tool to delete a file or folder at the specified path in Dropbox. Use when you need to permanently remove a file or folder and all its contents.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: Path in the user's Dropbox to delete. The path must start with a slash.

inputs.name: parent_rev
inputs.about: Perform delete if given 'rev' matches the existing file's latest 'rev'. This field does not support deleting a folder.

tools.name: Delete file or folder (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use DeleteFile instead. Permanently and irreversibly deletes the file or folder at the specified path in Dropbox. Folder deletion is recursive — all nested contents are removed. Always obtain explicit user confirmation before calling, especially for folders. Requires the `files.content.write` scope.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path to the file or folder to delete

tools.name: Delete file requests
tools.description: Tool to delete a batch of closed file requests in Dropbox. Use when you need to remove multiple file requests that are no longer needed. Only closed file requests can be deleted; attempting to delete open file requests will fail.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: List of file request IDs to delete. Only closed file requests can be deleted.

tools.name: Delete manual contacts batch
tools.description: Tool to delete specific manually added contacts from Dropbox by their email addresses. Use when you need to remove contacts that were manually added to a user's Dropbox account.

inputs.name: email_addresses
inputs.about: List of email addresses of manually added contacts to delete. Must be valid email addresses.

inputs.name: dropbox_api_select_user
inputs.about: Team member ID (format: dbmid:...) to specify which team member's contacts to delete. Required when using team OAuth tokens. Optional for individual accounts.

tools.name: Permanently delete archived team folder
tools.description: Tool to permanently delete an archived team folder in Dropbox. Use when you need to permanently remove an archived team folder and all its contents. The team folder must be archived before it can be permanently deleted.

inputs.name: team_folder_id
inputs.about: The ID of the team folder to permanently delete. The team folder must be archived before it can be permanently deleted. You can get this from list team folders action.

tools.name: Delete team group
tools.description: Tool to delete a Dropbox team group. Use when you need to remove a team group. Note that this requires team admin permissions and the group cannot be system-managed.

inputs.name: group_id
inputs.about: The Dropbox group ID. Required when selector_type is 'group_id'. Example: 'g:e18cdeb8c1e9c0280000000000000053'

inputs.name: selector_type
inputs.about: The type of selector to use for identifying the group. 'group_id' - Select group by Dropbox group ID. 'group_external_id' - Select group by external ID.

inputs.name: group_external_id
inputs.about: The external ID of the group. Required when selector_type is 'group_external_id'. This is the ID from an external system that has been associated with the Dropbox group.

tools.name: Delete team member profile photo
tools.description: Tool to delete a team member's profile photo. Use when you need to remove the profile picture of a team member. Requires team admin permissions.

inputs.name: user
inputs.about: The team member whose profile photo should be deleted.

tools.name: Delete team members secondary emails
tools.description: Tool to delete secondary email addresses from Dropbox team members. Use when you need to remove secondary emails from one or more team members. Requires team member management permissions.

inputs.name: emails_to_delete
inputs.about: List of users and their secondary emails to delete. Each entry specifies a user and which secondary emails to remove from that user

tools.name: Download Folder as Zip
tools.description: Tool to download a folder from Dropbox as a zip file. Use when you need to download an entire folder structure with multiple files. The folder must be less than 20 GB in size with any single file less than 4 GB, and the resulting zip must have fewer than 10,000 total entries.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path to the folder to download as a zip file. Must be a folder path, not a single file. The folder must be less than 20 GB in size with any single file less than 4 GB. The resulting zip must have fewer than 10,000 total file and folder entries.

tools.name: Export File
tools.description: Export Dropbox files, including non-downloadable files such as Paper documents, and return UTF-8 text and metadata; text is truncated beyond 500,000 characters. An optional mode requests a temporary link to the original file when downloadable, otherwise returning exported text; requires files.content.read.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.about: 'return_text': return exported text directly (truncated safely if very large). 'store_and_link': create a temporary Dropbox download link to the original file.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path of the file to be exported. Supports Dropbox path (e.g., '/folder/file.paper'), id:..., rev:..., or ns:... notation. Use this for non-downloadable files like Dropbox Paper documents.

inputs.name: export_format
inputs.about: The file format to export to. Common values: 'markdown', 'html', 'plain_text'. If not specified, the default format for the file type will be used. For Dropbox Paper, default is 'markdown'.

tools.name: Search files and folders
tools.description: Tool to search for files and folders in Dropbox by name or content. Use when you need to find items matching a search query within a specific path or across the entire Dropbox.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.about: Search mode for Dropbox files search.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path in the user's Dropbox to search. Should probably be a folder. Use empty string to search the entire Dropbox.

inputs.name: query
inputs.about: The string to search for. The search string is split on spaces into multiple tokens. For file name searching, the last token is used for prefix matching (e.g., 'bat c' matches 'bat cave' but not 'batman car').

inputs.name: start
inputs.about: The starting index within the search results (used for paging). Default is 0.

inputs.name: max_results
inputs.about: The maximum number of search results to return. Default is 100, max is 1000.

tools.name: Finish upload session
tools.description: Tool to finish an upload session and save the uploaded data to the given file path. Use when completing a multi-part upload after using upload_session/start and upload_session/append. A single request should not upload more than 150 MiB. The maximum size of a file one can upload to an upload session is 2,199,019,061,248 bytes.

inputs.name: commit
inputs.about: Contains the path and other optional modifiers for the commit.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: Cursor information containing the session_id and current offset in bytes.

inputs.name: content
inputs.about: Final file data to append before finishing the session. Can be omitted if no additional data needs to be appended.

tools.name: Finish batch upload sessions
tools.description: Tool to commit many files at once into a user's Dropbox after uploading file contents via upload_session/start and upload_session/append. Use when you need to finish multiple upload sessions in a single request. Returns an async_job_id which can be used with upload_session/finish_batch/check to poll for completion. Maximum 1000 entries per request.

inputs.name: entries
inputs.about: List of upload sessions to finish. Each entry contains cursor information and commit parameters. Maximum 1000 entries per request.

tools.name: Get about me
tools.description: Tool to get information about the current user's Dropbox account. Use when you need to retrieve account details like email, name, or account type. Useful for verifying authenticated account identity before destructive operations in multi-account setups. Note: successful response does not imply access to all shared or team folders; path-specific permission errors from other tools indicate missing folder-level permissions, not empty results.

tools.name: Get account
tools.description: Tool to get information about a user's Dropbox account using their account ID. Use when you need to retrieve account details for a specific user.

inputs.name: account_id
inputs.about: A user's account identifier. Can be obtained from get_current_account endpoint.

tools.name: Get account batch
tools.description: Tool to get information about multiple user accounts in a single request. At most 300 accounts may be queried per request. Use when you need to retrieve details for multiple Dropbox users efficiently.

inputs.name: account_ids
inputs.about: List of user account identifiers. Should not contain any duplicate account IDs. Maximum 300 accounts per request.

tools.name: Get available team member roles
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all available team member roles for the connected Dropbox team. Use when you need to discover what roles can be assigned to team members (e.g., Team, Billing, Report, Content, Security, User management, Support).

tools.name: Get copy reference
tools.description: Tool to get a copy reference to a file or folder. Use when you need to generate a reference string that can be used to copy the file or folder to another user's Dropbox via copy_reference/save.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path to the file or folder you want to get a copy reference to. This path is case-sensitive.

tools.name: Get file lock batch
tools.description: Tool to return lock metadata for multiple files in a single batch request. Use when you need to check the lock status of up to 1000 files at once.

inputs.name: entries
inputs.about: List of files to check lock status for. Maximum 1000 entries per request.

tools.name: Get shared file metadata batch
tools.description: Tool to retrieve metadata for multiple shared files in a single batch request. Use when you need to get information about shared file permissions, access levels, owners, and sharing policies for multiple files at once.

inputs.name: files
inputs.about: List of files to query. Each can be a file ID (e.g., 'id:7bh4zBmgZoAAAAAAAAAAFg') or a path (e.g., '/path/to/file.txt'). Maximum 100 files per request.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: A list of FileActions corresponding to FilePermissions that should appear in the response's permissions field describing the actions the authenticated user can perform on the files.

tools.name: Get file preview
tools.description: Tool to get a preview for a file. PDF previews are generated for document formats (.ai, .doc, .docx, .eps, .ppt, .pptx, etc.), and HTML previews are generated for spreadsheet formats (.csv, .xls, .xlsx, etc.). Use when you need to view file content without downloading the original file. Returns error for unsupported file types.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path of the file to preview. Supported preview formats: PDF previews (.ai, .doc, .docm, .docx, .eps, .gdoc, .gslides, .odp, .odt, .pps, .ppsm, .ppsx, .ppt, .pptm, .pptx, .rtf); HTML previews (.csv, .ods, .xls, .xlsm, .gsheet, .xlsx).

tools.name: Get file request details
tools.description: Tool to retrieve details of an existing file request by ID. Use when you need to check the status, URL, deadline, or other details of a specific file request.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the file request to retrieve.

tools.name: Get file or folder tags
tools.description: Tool to get list of tags assigned to files or folders in Dropbox. Use when you need to retrieve tags for one or more items. This endpoint does not support apps with the app folder permission.

inputs.name: paths
inputs.about: List of file or folder paths to get tags for (e.g., ["/Documents/report.pdf", "/Photos/image.jpg"]). Maximum of 1000 paths per request.

tools.name: Get folder state cursor
tools.description: Tool to get a cursor representing the current state of a folder without listing its contents. Use when you only need to track future changes to a folder, not retrieve existing files. This is more efficient than list_folder for setting up change monitoring or sync functionality.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path to the folder. Use "" (empty string) for the root folder, or a path like "/folder/subfolder". Also accepts folder IDs (e.g., "id:abc123xyz").

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: The maximum number of results to return per request when using this cursor with list_folder/continue. If not specified, the API uses a default.

inputs.name: recursive
inputs.about: If true, the cursor will include all subfolders and their contents recursively. If false, only the immediate contents are tracked.

inputs.name: shared_link
inputs.about: Shared link information for listing folder contents.

inputs.name: include_deleted
inputs.about: If true, deleted files and folders will be included when using this cursor to track changes.

inputs.name: include_media_info
inputs.about: If true, media metadata (dimensions, location, etc.) will be included for photo and video files when using this cursor.

inputs.name: include_mounted_folders
inputs.about: If true, results will include entries under mounted folders (app folders, shared folders, team folders).

inputs.name: include_property_groups
inputs.about: Template filter for property groups.

inputs.name: include_has_explicit_shared_members
inputs.about: If true, results will include a flag indicating whether each file or folder has explicit shared members.

tools.name: Get JWKS
tools.description: Tool to retrieve JSON Web Key Set containing public verification keys for Dropbox signed ID tokens. Use when you need to verify JWT signatures from Dropbox OpenID Connect authentication.

tools.name: Get file or folder metadata
tools.description: Fetch metadata for a Dropbox file or folder by path, including identifiers, type and attributes, without enumerating folder contents. The root folder path is not supported.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path of a file or folder on Dropbox (e.g., "/Documents/report.pdf"). Note: The root folder ("" or "/") is not supported by this endpoint.

inputs.name: include_deleted
inputs.about: If true, DeletedMetadata will be returned for deleted files or folders. Otherwise, deleted items will return an error.

inputs.name: include_media_info
inputs.about: If true, FileMetadata.media_info is set for photo and video files, providing additional metadata like dimensions and location.

inputs.name: include_has_explicit_shared_members
inputs.about: If true, the result will include a flag indicating whether the file has any explicit shared members.

tools.name: Get file or folder metadata (alpha)
tools.description: Tool to fetch metadata for a file or folder using the alpha endpoint. Use when you need metadata with advanced property filtering or custom property template support.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path of a file or folder on Dropbox (e.g., "/Documents/report.pdf"). Use "" or "/" for the root folder.

inputs.name: include_deleted
inputs.about: If true, DeletedMetadata will be returned for deleted files or folders. Otherwise, deleted items will return an error.

inputs.name: include_media_info
inputs.about: If true, FileMetadata.media_info is set for photo and video files, providing additional metadata like dimensions and location.

inputs.name: include_property_groups
inputs.about: Filter for property template IDs.

inputs.name: include_has_explicit_shared_members
inputs.about: If true, the result will include a flag indicating whether the file has any explicit shared members.

tools.name: Get OpenID config
tools.description: Tool to retrieve Dropbox's OpenID Connect discovery document describing supported OAuth 2.0 and OIDC parameters. Use when you need to discover Dropbox's OAuth configuration endpoints and capabilities.

tools.name: Get shared file metadata
tools.description: Tool to retrieve metadata for a shared file in Dropbox. Use when you need to get information about a shared file's permissions, access levels, owner, and sharing policies.

inputs.name: file
inputs.about: The file to query. Can be a file ID (e.g., 'id:7bh4zBmgZoAAAAAAAAAAFg') or a path.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: A list of FileActions corresponding to FilePermissions that should appear in the response's permissions field describing the actions the authenticated user can perform on the file.

tools.name: Get shared folder metadata
tools.description: Tool to retrieve metadata for a specific shared folder by its ID. Use when you need detailed information about a shared folder including access level, policies, owner, paths, and permissions.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: A list of FolderActions corresponding to FolderPermissions that should appear in the response's permissions field describing the actions the authenticated user can perform on the folder

inputs.name: shared_folder_id
inputs.about: The ID for the shared folder

tools.name: Download file from shared link
tools.description: Tool to download a file from a Dropbox shared link. Use when you have a shared link URL and need to retrieve the actual file content. This endpoint works with shared links to files; for shared links to folders, use the path parameter to specify which file within the folder to download.

inputs.name: url
inputs.about: URL of the shared link to download the file from.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: If the shared link is to a folder, this parameter can be used to retrieve a specific file or sub-folder in this folder. Path must start with '/'.

inputs.name: link_password
inputs.about: If the shared link has a password, this parameter can be used to provide it.

tools.name: Get shared link metadata
tools.description: Tool to resolve a Dropbox shared link URL into structured metadata. Use when the user provides a shared link and you need to determine what it points to (file vs folder) and obtain canonical identifiers (id, path) to enable follow-on operations.

inputs.name: url
inputs.about: The shared link URL to retrieve metadata for.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: If the shared link is to a folder, this parameter can be used to retrieve metadata for a specific file or sub-folder in this folder. A relative path should be used.

inputs.name: link_password
inputs.about: If the shared link has a password, this parameter can be used to provide it.

tools.name: Get space usage
tools.description: Tool to get space usage information for the current user's Dropbox account. Use when you need to check storage usage, available space, or quota information.

tools.name: Get team feature values
tools.description: Tool to get values for one or more team features. Use when you need to check team capabilities like upload rate limits, shared team root availability, file events, or selective sync status.

inputs.name: features
inputs.about: A list of features to get values for. At least one feature must be included. Available features: 'upload_api_rate_limit', 'has_team_shared_dropbox', 'has_team_file_events', 'has_team_selective_sync'.

tools.name: Get team folder info
tools.description: Tool to retrieve metadata for team folders. Returns information about folder status, sync settings, and properties for the specified team folder IDs. Use when you need to check the status or configuration of one or more team folders.

inputs.name: team_folder_ids
inputs.about: The list of team folder IDs to retrieve metadata for. Must contain at least one ID.

tools.name: Get team groups info
tools.description: Tool to retrieve information about one or more team groups by their IDs or external IDs. Use when you need to get details about specific groups including name, member count, management type, and creation time.

inputs.name: group_ids
inputs.about: List of Dropbox group IDs. Required when selector_type is 'group_ids'. Example: ['g:e18cdeb8c1e9c0280000000000000053', 'g:e18cdeb8c1e9c0280000000000000054']

inputs.name: selector_type
inputs.about: The type of selector to use for identifying groups. 'group_ids' - Select groups by Dropbox group IDs. 'group_external_ids' - Select groups by external IDs.

inputs.name: group_external_ids
inputs.about: List of external group IDs. Required when selector_type is 'group_external_ids'. These are IDs from an external system that have been associated with Dropbox groups.

tools.name: Get team groups job status
tools.description: Tool to check the status of an asynchronous team groups job in Dropbox. Use when you have an async_job_id from a previous team groups operation (like groups_delete) and need to poll its completion status.

inputs.name: async_job_id
inputs.about: Id of the asynchronous job. This is the value of a response returned from the method that launched the job (e.g., from team_groups_delete).

tools.name: Get team info
tools.description: Tool to retrieve information about a Dropbox team. Use when you need to get team details such as team name, ID, licensed user counts, or team policies.

tools.name: Get team audit log events
tools.description: Tool to retrieve team audit log events from Dropbox. Use when you need to access team activity logs, audit trails, or monitor team events. Supports filtering by time range and event category, with pagination for large result sets.

inputs.name: time
inputs.about: Time range filter for events.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Maximum number of events to return per request. Default is 1000, maximum is 1000.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: Cursor for pagination, obtained from a previous response. Use this to retrieve the next page of results.

inputs.name: category
inputs.about: Event category filter to limit results (e.g., 'apps', 'devices', 'domains', 'file_operations', 'file_requests', 'groups', 'logins', 'members', 'paper', 'passwords', 'sharing', 'team_folders', 'team_policies').

tools.name: Get team log events (continue)
tools.description: Tool to paginate through team audit log events using a cursor from team_log/get_events. Use when you have a cursor from a previous call and need to retrieve the next batch of team events.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: The cursor returned by a previous call to team_log/get_events or team_log/get_events/continue. This cursor is used to paginate through all team events.

tools.name: Get team member custom quota
tools.description: Tool to retrieve custom storage quotas for team members. Use when you need to check which team members have custom quota allocations and their quota amounts. Requires team admin credentials.

inputs.name: users
inputs.about: List of team member identifiers to retrieve custom quota for. Each member must be identified by exactly one of: team_member_id, external_id, or email. Maximum of 1000 users per request. An empty list returns all users with custom quotas.

tools.name: Get team members add job status v2
tools.description: Tool to poll the status of an asynchronous team member addition job. Use when you have an async_job_id from team/members/add_v2 and need to check if the member addition has completed. Returns 'in_progress', 'complete' with per-member results, or 'failed' with error details.

inputs.name: async_job_id
inputs.about: Id of the asynchronous job returned from team/members/add_v2. This is used to poll the status of the asynchronous request.

tools.name: Get team members info
tools.description: Tool to retrieve information about multiple team members in a single request. Use when you need to get details like email, name, status, role, and account information for one or more team members. Requires team admin credentials.

inputs.name: members
inputs.about: List of team member identifiers to retrieve information for. Each member must be identified by exactly one of: team_member_id, external_id, or email.

tools.name: Get property template for team
tools.description: Tool to get the schema for a specified property template for a team. Use when you need to retrieve the structure and field definitions of a team property template.

inputs.name: template_id
inputs.about: An identifier for a template added by route templates/add_for_user or templates/add_for_team. Typically in the format 'ptid:XXXXX'.

tools.name: Get temporary link
tools.description: Tool to get a one-click temporary (expiring) download link. Use when you need to share a Dropbox file directly without proxying content through this service. Only works for files, not folders. Returned URLs expire within hours and must be regenerated for future use; never treat them as permanent links. Requires `files.content.read` scope.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path or identifier of the file to get a temporary link for. Supports Dropbox path (e.g., '/folder/file.txt'), id:..., rev:..., or ns:... notation.

tools.name: Get temporary upload link
tools.description: Tool to get a one-time use temporary upload link to upload a file to Dropbox. Use when you need to perform a delayed upload where the file will be uploaded to the returned link via POST with Content-Type: application/octet-stream. The upload link is valid for up to 4 hours.

inputs.name: duration
inputs.about: Link validity period in seconds. Maximum is 4 hours (14400 seconds).

inputs.name: commit_info
inputs.about: Upload configuration specifying destination path and upload behavior.

tools.name: Get thumbnail
tools.description: Tool to get a thumbnail for an image file. Use when you need to generate a thumbnail preview of an image. Supports jpg, jpeg, png, tiff, tif, gif, webp, ppm, and bmp files under 20MB.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.about: How to resize and crop the image. 'strict': scale down to fit within the given size. 'bestfit': scale down to fit within size or its transpose. 'fitone_bestfit': scale down to completely cover size or its transpose.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path to the image file you want to thumbnail. Must start with '/'.

inputs.name: size
inputs.about: The size for the thumbnail image. Options range from 32x32 pixels to 2048x1536 pixels.

inputs.name: format
inputs.about: The format for the thumbnail image. Use 'jpeg' for photos (default), 'png' for screenshots and digital arts.

tools.name: Get thumbnail batch
tools.description: Tool to get thumbnails for multiple image files in a single batch request. Use when you need to generate thumbnail previews for up to 25 images at once. Supports jpg, jpeg, png, tiff, tif, gif, webp, ppm, and bmp files under 20MB.

inputs.name: entries
inputs.about: List of files to get thumbnails for. Maximum 25 entries per request.

tools.name: Get thumbnail v2
tools.description: Tool to get a thumbnail for an image file. Use when you need to generate a thumbnail preview of an image. Supports jpg, jpeg, png, tiff, tif, gif, webp, ppm, and bmp files under 20MB. Can access files via direct path or shared link.

inputs.name: url
inputs.about: The shared link URL (required when resource_type is 'link').

inputs.name: mode
inputs.about: How to resize and crop the image. 'strict': scale down to fit within the given size. 'bestfit': scale down to fit within size or its transpose. 'fitone_bestfit': scale down to completely cover size or its transpose.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path to the image file (required when resource_type is 'path'). Must start with '/'.

inputs.name: size
inputs.about: The size for the thumbnail image. Options range from 32x32 pixels to 2048x1536 pixels.

inputs.name: format
inputs.about: The format for the thumbnail image. Use 'jpeg' for photos, 'png' for screenshots and digital arts.

inputs.name: link_path
inputs.about: Optional relative path within shared folder (only used with resource_type='link' when link points to a folder).

inputs.name: resource_type
inputs.about: Type of resource: 'path' for direct file path or 'link' for shared link.

tools.name: Get user features
tools.description: Tool to get a list of feature values configured for the current Dropbox account. Use when you need to check which features are enabled, such as paper_as_files or file_locking.

inputs.name: features
inputs.about: A list of features to get values for. Available features: 'paper_as_files' (information about how Paper files are stored), 'file_locking' (whether users can lock files in shared directories).

tools.name: List member space limits excluded users (continue)
tools.description: Tool to paginate through team members excluded from space limits using a cursor from a previous list call. Use when you have a cursor from the initial excluded users list endpoint and need to retrieve the next batch of excluded team members.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: The cursor returned by a previous call to list member space limits excluded users. This cursor is used to paginate through all excluded users. Must come from a previous call to /2/team/member_space_limits/excluded_users/list or /2/team/member_space_limits/excluded_users/list/continue.

tools.name: List file members
tools.description: List users, groups and invitees with access to a shared file, including access levels and optionally inherited members and requested permissions. Results may be incomplete when a continuation cursor is returned.

inputs.name: file
inputs.about: The file for which you want to see members. Can be a file ID (starting with 'id:') or a file path (starting with '/').

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Number of members to return max per query. Must be between 1 and 300.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: The actions for which to return permissions on a member. Valid values: 'leave_a_copy', 'make_editor', 'make_owner', 'make_viewer', 'make_viewer_no_comment', 'remove'.

inputs.name: include_inherited
inputs.about: Whether to include members who only have access from a parent shared folder. Defaults to true.

tools.name: List file members batch
tools.description: Retrieve sharing members for multiple files in one request, including users, groups, invitees and member counts or per-file access errors. The request defaults to at most 10 members per file and permits a limit of up to 20.

inputs.name: files
inputs.about: Files for which to return members. Can be file IDs (starting with 'id:') or paths (starting with '/'). Maximum 100 files per request.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Number of members to return max per query per file. Defaults to 10 if not specified. Maximum 20.

tools.name: List file requests
tools.description: List a page of file requests owned by the current user, including their status and details. The response includes a cursor and indicates whether more results are available.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Maximum number of file requests to return. Default: 1000.

tools.name: List file requests (continue)
tools.description: Tool to paginate through file requests using a cursor from a previous list call. Use when you have a cursor from /2/file_requests/list or /2/file_requests/list/continue and need to retrieve the next batch of file requests.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: The cursor returned by a previous call to list file requests. This cursor is used to paginate through all file requests. Must come from a previous call to /2/file_requests/list or /2/file_requests/list/continue.

tools.name: List file revisions
tools.description: Retrieve the revision history for a file to inspect past versions or track changes over time.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.about: Mode for listing revisions.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path to the file you want to see the revisions of (e.g., "/Documents/report.pdf"). Must be a valid file path in Dropbox.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: The maximum number of revision entries returned. Default is 10, minimum is 1, maximum is 100.

tools.name: List files in folder
tools.description: Tool to list files and folders in a specified Dropbox directory. Use when you need to see the contents of a folder, including subfolders if recursive is true. When the response contains `has_more=true`, continue fetching with the returned cursor until `has_more=false` — stopping early misses entries in large folders. Response entries include both files and folders; use the `.tag` field on each entry to distinguish item types.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The folder path (e.g., "/europe/invoices") or folder ID (e.g., "id:aBcDeFgH123") to list contents from. Use "" (empty string) for the root folder. No trailing slashes or whitespace allowed — malformed paths can silently produce empty results. Prefer paths from `path_display` or `path_lower` fields i

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: The maximum number of results to return per request. Default is 2000. Max is 2000.

inputs.name: recursive
inputs.about: If true, recursively lists contents of nested subfolders; otherwise, lists only immediate contents. Large or broad folder trees with recursive=true can produce very large responses and high latency; use only when full hierarchy is explicitly needed.

inputs.name: include_deleted
inputs.about: If true, includes deleted (but potentially recoverable) files and folders in the listing.

inputs.name: include_media_info
inputs.about: If true, includes media metadata (e.g., dimensions, location) for photo and video files.

inputs.name: include_non_downloadable_files
inputs.about: If true, includes non-downloadable files (e.g., Google Docs, Dropbox Paper) in the listing.

tools.name: List folder continue
tools.description: Tool to continue paginating through folder contents using a cursor from list_folder. Use when has_more is true to retrieve remaining entries.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: The cursor returned by your last call to list_folder or list_folder/continue. Use this to paginate through all files and retrieve updates to the folder.

tools.name: List folder members
tools.description: Tool to list members of a shared folder, including users, groups, and invitees. Use when you need to retrieve information about who has access to a specific shared folder and their permission levels.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: The maximum number of results that include members, groups and invitees to return per request

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: List indicating whether each returned member will include a boolean value showing if the current user can perform the MemberAction on the member. Valid values: 'leave_a_copy', 'make_editor', 'make_owner', 'make_viewer', 'make_viewer_no_comment', 'remove'

inputs.name: shared_folder_id
inputs.about: The ID for the shared folder

tools.name: List folder members continue
tools.description: Tool to continue paginating through shared folder members using a cursor from list_folder_members. Use when cursor is present in list_folder_members response to retrieve remaining member entries.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: The cursor returned by your last call to list_folder_members or list_folder_members/continue. Use this to paginate through all shared folder members.

tools.name: List folder contents (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use ListFilesInFolder instead. Retrieves a list of folders, files, and deleted entries from a specified Dropbox path.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: Path to the folder (e.g., "" for root, "/folder/subfolder", or "id:abc123xyz"). If a path string, it must start with / and not end with / or whitespace.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Maximum number of folder entries to return per request; an approximate upper bound.

inputs.name: recursive
inputs.about: Whether to include folders in nested subfolders (True) or only immediate subfolders (False) Combining with a high `limit` or broad `path` can yield very large responses; scope `path` narrowly to keep result sets manageable.

inputs.name: include_deleted
inputs.about: Whether to include folders that have been deleted but may be recoverable

tools.name: List shared folders continue
tools.description: Tool to continue paginating through shared folders using a cursor from list_folders. Use when the cursor is present in list_folders response to retrieve remaining shared folder entries.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: The cursor returned by the previous call to list_folders or list_folders/continue. Use this to paginate through all shared folders.

tools.name: List member linked apps
tools.description: Tool to list all applications linked to a specific team member's account. Use when you need to audit or review which third-party applications have been authorized by a particular team member.

inputs.name: team_member_id
inputs.about: The team member ID. Can be obtained from team/members/list endpoint.

tools.name: List excluded users from space limits
tools.description: Tool to list team members excluded from space limits. Use when you need to view which users are exempt from storage quotas. This is a team-level operation requiring team admin authentication.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Number of results to return per call. If not specified, all excluded users will be returned.

tools.name: List mountable folders
tools.description: Tool to list all shared folders the current user can mount or unmount. Use when discovering mountable shared folders (unmounted folders can be identified by absence of path_lower field). This endpoint does not support apps with the app folder permission.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Maximum number of mountable folders to return per request. If not specified, the API will use its default limit.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: List of FolderActions corresponding to FolderPermissions that should appear in the response's SharedFolderMetadata.permissions field, describing the actions the authenticated user can perform on the folder.

tools.name: List mountable folders continue
tools.description: Tool to paginate through mountable shared folders using a cursor. Use when you have a cursor from a previous call to list_mountable_folders or list_mountable_folders/continue and need to retrieve the next batch of folders.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: The cursor returned by a previous call to list_mountable_folders or list_mountable_folders/continue. Use this to paginate through all mountable shared folders.

tools.name: List Paper docs
tools.description: Tool to return the list of all Paper docs according to filter and sort specifications. Use when you need to retrieve Paper document IDs for further operations. To iterate through full pagination, pass the cursor to docs/list/continue.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Size limit per batch. The maximum number of docs that can be retrieved per batch is 1000. Higher value results in invalid arguments error.

inputs.name: sort_by
inputs.about: Allows user to specify how the Paper docs should be sorted. 'accessed' sorts by last accessed time, 'modified' sorts by last modified time, 'created' sorts by creation time.

inputs.name: filter_by
inputs.about: Allows user to specify how the Paper docs should be filtered. 'docs_accessed' fetches all Paper doc IDs that the user has ever accessed. 'docs_created' fetches only the Paper doc IDs that the user has created.

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: Allows user to specify the sort order of the result. 'ascending' sorts in ascending order, 'descending' sorts in descending order.

tools.name: List Paper documents (continue)
tools.description: Tool to continue paginating through Paper documents using a cursor from paper/docs/list. Use when has_more is true to retrieve remaining Paper documents. Note: This endpoint continues to work for older Paper content; check user features to determine Paper version.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: The cursor obtained from paper/docs/list or paper/docs/list/continue. Allows for pagination through all Paper documents.

tools.name: List received files
tools.description: List files directly shared with the current user, excluding files received via shared folders or unclaimed invitations. Returns a page of results and may provide a cursor for additional files.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Number of files to return max per query. Defaults to 100 if no limit is specified. Must be between 1 and 300.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: A list of FileActions corresponding to FilePermissions that should appear in the response's SharedFileMetadata.permissions field describing the actions the authenticated user can perform on the file.

tools.name: List shared folders
tools.description: Lists shared folders accessible to the authenticated user, including folder name, ID, access level, and paths when available. Returns a page of results and a cursor when further results are available.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Maximum number of shared folders to return per request

tools.name: List shared links
tools.description: Tool to list existing shared links for the current user, optionally filtered by path. Use when you need to discover or reuse existing shared links to avoid creating duplicates or to check what links already exist for a file or folder. Supports pagination via cursor for large result sets.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The path to the file or folder to list shared links for. If omitted, returns all shared links for the current user. If provided, returns links that grant access to the specified path (including parent folder links unless direct_only is true). Supports Dropbox path notation (e.g., '/folder/file.txt')

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: The cursor returned by a previous call to this endpoint. Use this to retrieve additional results when 'has_more' is true. The API returns a maximum of ~200 links per call.

inputs.name: direct_only
inputs.about: If true, only return direct links to the specified path. If false or omitted, also include links to parent folders. Only relevant when 'path' is specified.

tools.name: List team sharing allowlist
tools.description: Tool to list Approve List entries for a team from newest to oldest. Use when you need to retrieve allowed domains and emails for team sharing.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: The number of entries to fetch at one time. Maximum and default is 1000.

tools.name: List team devices
tools.description: Tool to list all device sessions of a team including web sessions, desktop clients, and mobile clients. Use when you need to audit team devices, view active sessions, or monitor device activity across the team. Supports pagination via cursor for large result sets. Requires team admin credentials.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: Pagination cursor for retrieving additional results. At the first call to list_team_devices, the cursor shouldn't be passed. Then, if the result includes a cursor, subsequent requests should include the received cursor to retrieve the next sub-list of team devices.

inputs.name: include_web_sessions
inputs.about: Whether to list web sessions of the team members. If omitted, defaults to the API's default behavior.

inputs.name: include_mobile_clients
inputs.about: Whether to list mobile clients of the team members. If omitted, defaults to the API's default behavior.

inputs.name: include_desktop_clients
inputs.about: Whether to list desktop clients of the team members. If omitted, defaults to the API's default behavior.

tools.name: List team folders
tools.description: List team folders for a Dropbox Business team. Returns one page of folder metadata with a cursor and an indication of whether more folders are available.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Maximum number of team folders to return per request

tools.name: List team folders continue
tools.description: Tool to continue paginating through team folders using a cursor from team_folder/list. Use when the cursor is present in list_team_folders response to retrieve remaining team folder entries.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: The cursor returned by the previous call to team_folder/list or team_folder/list/continue. Use this to paginate through all team folders.

tools.name: List team group members
tools.description: Tool to list members of a Dropbox team group. Use when you need to retrieve the list of team members who belong to a specific group. Returns member profiles with email, status, and access information.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Maximum number of members to return per request. Must be between 1 and 1000.

inputs.name: group_id
inputs.about: The Dropbox group ID. Required when selector_type is 'group_id'. Example: 'g:e18cdeb8c1e9c0280000000000000003'

inputs.name: selector_type
inputs.about: The type of selector to use for identifying the group. 'group_id' - Select group by Dropbox group ID. 'group_external_id' - Select group by external ID.

inputs.name: group_external_id
inputs.about: The external ID of the group. Required when selector_type is 'group_external_id'. This is the ID from an external system that has been associated with the Dropbox group.

tools.name: List team groups
tools.description: List groups on a Dropbox team, returning a page of group metadata including group ID, name, and member count when available. The response includes a cursor and indicates whether more groups are available.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Number of groups to return per call. If not specified, all groups are returned.

tools.name: List team groups continue
tools.description: Tool to continue listing team groups using a cursor from team/groups/list. Use when you have a cursor from a previous team groups list call and need to retrieve the next batch of groups.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: The cursor returned by team/groups/list. Indicates from what point to get the next set of groups.

tools.name: List team group members continue
tools.description: Tool to continue listing team group members using a cursor from team/groups/members/list. Use when you have a cursor from a previous group members list call and need to retrieve the next batch of members.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: The cursor returned by team/groups/members/list. Indicates from what point to get the next set of group members.

tools.name: List members linked apps
tools.description: Tool to list all applications linked to team members' accounts. Use when you need to audit or review which third-party applications have been authorized by team members. Supports pagination for large teams.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: At the first call, the cursor shouldn't be passed. Then, if the result includes a cursor, subsequent requests should include the received cursor to receive the next sub-list of team applications.

tools.name: List team member devices
tools.description: Tool to list all device sessions of a team's member, including web sessions, desktop clients, and mobile clients. Use when you need to retrieve information about a team member's active devices and sessions.

inputs.name: team_member_id
inputs.about: The team's member id. Can be obtained from team/members/list endpoint.

inputs.name: include_web_sessions
inputs.about: Whether to list web sessions of the team's member. Defaults to true.

inputs.name: include_mobile_clients
inputs.about: Whether to list linked mobile devices of the team's member. Defaults to true.

inputs.name: include_desktop_clients
inputs.about: Whether to list linked desktop devices of the team's member. Defaults to true.

tools.name: List team members
tools.description: List a batch of Dropbox team members, including their status, roles and contact details. The response includes a cursor and indicates whether more members are available.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Number of results to return per call. Maximum is 1000. If not specified, the server will use a default value.

inputs.name: include_removed
inputs.about: Whether to return members who have been removed from the team. If true, includes removed members in the results.

tools.name: List team members continue (v2)
tools.description: Tool to continue listing team members using a cursor from team/members/list or team/members/list/continue_v2. Use when you have a cursor from a previous team members list call and need to retrieve the next batch of members.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: The cursor returned by team/members/list or team/members/list/continue_v2. Indicates from what point to get the next set of members.

tools.name: List team namespaces
tools.description: List team-accessible namespaces in a Dropbox Business team, including team folders, shared folders, member home namespaces, and app folders. Results may be paginated; use the returned cursor to retrieve further pages.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Specifying a value here has no effect. The parameter is included for API compatibility but is not functional.

tools.name: List team namespaces continue
tools.description: Tool to continue paginating through team-accessible namespaces using a cursor from team/namespaces/list. Use when you have a cursor and need to retrieve the next batch of team namespaces.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: Cursor returned by a previous call to team/namespaces/list or team/namespaces/list/continue. Use this to paginate through all team-accessible namespaces.

tools.name: List team sharing allowlist continue
tools.description: Tool to continue paginating through team sharing allowlist entries using a cursor. Use when you have a cursor from a previous sharing_allowlist/list or sharing_allowlist/list/continue call and need to retrieve the next batch of allowed domains and emails.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: The cursor returned by a previous call to sharing_allowlist/list or sharing_allowlist/list/continue. Use this to paginate through all allowlist entries.

tools.name: List property templates for team
tools.description: List identifiers of custom file property templates available at the team level. Requires a Dropbox Business account with team-level authentication.

tools.name: List user templates
tools.description: Tool to get the template identifiers for a user. Use when you need to retrieve available custom file property templates that can be applied to files.

tools.name: Modify shared link settings
tools.description: Modify an existing Dropbox shared link's visibility, audience, access level, expiration, password protection or download settings. Audience choices include public, team and no one.

inputs.name: url
inputs.about: The URL of the shared link to modify. This must be a valid Dropbox shared link URL.

inputs.name: settings
inputs.about: The new settings to apply to the shared link. Only the specified fields will be updated; unspecified fields remain unchanged.

inputs.name: remove_expiration
inputs.about: If set to true, removes the expiration date from the shared link. This overrides any 'expires' value in settings.

tools.name: Mount shared folder
tools.description: Tool to mount a shared folder for the current user after they have been added as a member. Once mounted, the shared folder will appear in their Dropbox. Use when a user needs to access a shared folder that has been shared with them but not yet mounted.

inputs.name: shared_folder_id
inputs.about: The ID of the shared folder to mount.

tools.name: Move multiple files or folders in batch
tools.description: Tool to move multiple files or folders to different locations at once in Dropbox. Use when you need to relocate several items in a single operation. Note that case-only renaming is not supported. The operation may complete synchronously (returning status for each entry) or asynchronously (returning a job ID to check later with move_batch/check:2).

inputs.name: entries
inputs.about: List of entries to be moved. Each entry specifies a from_path and to_path. Minimum 1 entry, maximum 1000 entries.

inputs.name: autorename
inputs.about: If there's a conflict with any file, have the Dropbox server try to autorename that file to avoid the conflict. The default is false.

inputs.name: allow_ownership_transfer
inputs.about: Allow moves by owner even if it would result in an ownership transfer for the content being moved. The default is false.

tools.name: Move file or folder
tools.description: Move file or folder

inputs.name: to_path
inputs.about: Path in the user's Dropbox that is the destination. This path is case-sensitive.

inputs.name: from_path
inputs.about: Path in the user's Dropbox to be moved. This path is case-sensitive. Use canonical paths from metadata (path_display or path_lower) rather than manually constructed strings to avoid path/not_found errors.

inputs.name: autorename
inputs.about: If there's a conflict (e.g., a file with the same name already exists at the destination), have the Dropbox server try to auto-rename the file to avoid the conflict. The default is false. Leaving this false will cause the call to fail outright when a name conflict exists at the destination.

inputs.name: allow_shared_folder
inputs.about: If true, allows moving shared folders. The default is false.

inputs.name: allow_ownership_transfer
inputs.about: Allow moves by owner even if it would result in an ownership transfer for the content being moved. This does not apply to copies. The default is false.

tools.name: Overwrite file properties
tools.description: Tool to overwrite property groups associated with a file or folder. Use when you need to force apply or replace custom property values for specific templates on a file.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: A unique identifier for the file or folder. Can be a path (e.g., '/test_file.txt') or a file ID.

inputs.name: property_groups
inputs.about: The property groups to force apply. This operation will overwrite existing property groups for the specified templates.

inputs.name: Dropbox-API-Select-User
inputs.about: Team member ID (format: dbmid:...) required when using team tokens. Specifies which team member's account to operate on.

tools.name: Read a file
